title: Al-Muta'ali, the Most Exalted
tomorrow: is goodness about facing the right way, or something else?

cards: Some people count stairs. Some take them two at a time to the top of the bleachers and stand there, arms up, like they own the stadium. Yesterday's question asked why anyone would say God is greatest on the way up.
The answer comes from Jabir, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, in Sahih al-Bukhari: when we went up, he says, we said Allahu akbar. When we came down, we said subhanallah.

teach.h: WHEN YOU CLIMB, NAME SOMEONE TALLER.
teach.b: Going up is exactly when a person starts to feel tall. So, as commentators explain it, the companions met each climb by naming someone taller: God is greater.
Coming down, into a valley, they said subhanallah, glory be to God, the One above every low place and every flaw. Today's Name holds both directions. Al-Muta'ali, the Most Exalted, high above all.
The Qur'an puts it at the end of a verse, in Pickthall's words: "He is the Knower of the invisible and the visible, the Great, the High Exalted." Now bring it into this week.
A climb isn't only a hill. It's a win: the acceptance, the promotion, the game, the yes you waited for. The habit of the companions doesn't ban the joy.
It just gives the high moment a word that points above it. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: the first thing out of your mouth at the top says where you think the top is.
For the companions, it was a little higher than where they stood.

how: Muslims on a journey or climbing stairs and hills may say Allahu akbar going up and subhanallah going down, following the companions' practice reported by Jabir.

o: the Victor, raised up high after battle
the Highest Place, where heaven is found
the Most Exalted, high above all things

games.q: what goes with what — tap the pairs.

s: saying Allahu akbar belongs only to formal prayer
the companions said it climbing; any going up is a place for it.
the companions said subhanallah going down
Jabir reports it in Bukhari: up, Allahu akbar; down, subhanallah.
the hadith tells people to hide their good news
it doesn't forbid joy; it gives the climb a word that points above it.

games.q: your cousin wins the regional science fair and freezes at the mic: 'i don't know what to say first.' what would the companions' habit give her?
o: start by pointing higher, then enjoy her moment fully.
say nothing about the win, since any word about it is pride.
thank only herself; she did the work, so the moment is hers.
games.why: going up, they said God is greater. the climb isn't hidden or refused; its first word just points above the top.

practice: Stand up slowly, and as you rise say Allahu akbar, God is greatest, softly or out loud. Sit back down saying subhanallah, glory be to God. Then let the sit stay with the One higher than every high moment you've had this year.

wordCard.voice: Al-Muta'ali. The Most Exalted: above all, above every height you reach and every low place you pass through.

orig.note: Arabic: the Most Exalted, high above all. it closes 13:9.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: exalted, a little higher than wherever you're standing, even at the top. Enjoy the view.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2993 (Jabir: going up we said Allahu akbar, going down we said subhanallah)

sources.q: He is the Knower of the invisible and the visible, the Great, the High Exalted.

sources.ref: Commentary on Bukhari 2993 (takbir on rising as humility at a height; tasbih descending)
